title: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server MLflow plugin -- T1005 model-name path traversal escapes model repository
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-47487 (CVSS 4.4 MEDIUM),
affecting NVIDIA Triton Inference Server for Linux's MLflow plugin.

The Triton MLflow plugin accepts a caller-supplied model name that is
used to construct a filesystem path under the configured model
repository, without confining the resulting path to stay within it. A
model name containing traversal sequences lets a caller cause files
OUTSIDE the model repository to be read, written to, or modified,
reachable via the MLflow plugin's model-management interface --
NVIDIA's own advisory frames the impact as denial of service and
information disclosure.

Detection logic flags an MLflow-plugin model-registration/load request
whose model-name parameter contains a path-traversal sequence (`../`)
or resolves outside the configured model repository -- the specific
artifact that turns an ordinary model-name string into a filesystem
escape.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (NVIDIA, via
NVIDIA's own product-security bulletin and NVD).
